text:
maria: quick check — CI started failing downstream with 401s when we switched to the windows-latest runner for the export script. node sdk streaming requests get "Authorization: Basic" but server rejects it. suspect secret encoding issue from the gha step. anyone seen this?
jon: yup, ran into something similar. windows cmd/powershell helpers sometimes add a BOM or CRLF when writing secrets out. what does your workflow step look like?
maria: this is the offending step: `- run: echo "API_KEY=$${{ secrets.API_KEY }}" > ./envfile` (on windows-latest). then we do `set -o allexport; source ./envfile; node app.js` in a later step.
ashley: echo + windows redirect is notorious. On windows `>` uses UTF-16 LE with BOM if run under pwsh, IIRC. That breaks Basic header base64 because extra bytes get encoded.
samir: quick repro: if API_KEY contains only ascii but file is UTF-16LE with BOM, `cat envfile` looks fine in terminal but `process.env['API_KEY']` when read by some runtimes includes a leading \uFEFF or trailing \r. that will 401.
maria: nice. any reliable fix that keeps secrets masked in logs?
jon: two easy fixes: (1) write file with Set-Content/Out-File flags to avoid BOM/newline, or (2) avoid writing to disk and export env var directly in gha using `echo "API_KEY=***" >> $GITHUB_ENV` but make sure you use proper escaping.
ashley: examples: in pwsh step use:
```
- run: |
    $k = $env:GITHUB_SECRET_API_KEY.Trim()
    Set-Content -Path ./envfile -Value "API_KEY=$k" -Encoding UTF8 -NoNewline
  shell: pwsh
```
That writes UTF8 w/o BOM and no trailing newline.
samir: if you must use Out-File, use `-Encoding utf8 -NoNewline` in recent pwsh. older rn `Out-File` defaults may add BOM.
maria: thanks — our workflow uses `run: echo` in a multi-line bash step but windows runner used pwsh shell variant. switching shell to bash for that step might also fix it.
jon: alternative runtime-side quickfix: trim before use. in node wrapper we do `const key = (process.env.API_KEY || '').replace(/^\uFEFF|\r|\n/g, '');` then base64. solves immediate 401s but better to fix at CI step.
ci-bot: mask applied to secrets in logs. :mask:
maria: one more oddity — streaming sockets with bad header sometimes hang instead of quick 401 during first token, so SDK retry logic confused. we saw a flurry of retries, and then rate limit.
samir: yep, streaming libs sometimes treat initial 401/connection reset as transient. worth adding explicit header validation at client bootstrap and fail fast.
ashley: created a tiny gha snippet in the repo under .github/actions/examples/avoid-bom.md with the Set-Content snippet and the node trim helper. will link in PR.
maria: awesome — PR incoming. thanks team :raised_hands:
